meta.title: Dilutive securities and stock-based compensation
meta.summary: Convertible bonds and preferred stock, induced conversions, stock warrants issued with bonds, stock options measured at fair value over the service period, restricted stock, employee stock purchase plans and stock appreciation rights.

videos.title: Convertible bonds
videos.take: Convertible debt is recorded as debt; on conversion, the carrying amount moves to equity with no gain or loss

scenes.say: Bluestem wants to borrow cheaply. Investors will accept a lower rate if they can swap their bonds for shares later.

sub: for a set number of shares
scenes.say: A convertible bond lets the holder exchange it for a fixed number of common shares. The conversion feature is worth something, so the interest rate is lower: Bluestem pays four percent instead of six.

scenes.heading: Issuing $1,000,000 at par
scenes.say: Under current US GAAP, most convertible debt is recorded entirely as a liability. The conversion option isn't separated, unless special features require it.

scenes.heading: Conversion: each $1,000 bond into 50 shares
rows: Paid-in capital in excess of par
scenes.say: When all bonds convert, holders receive 50,000 shares. Under the book value method, the bonds' carrying amount moves to equity: $50,000 at par and $950,000 to paid-in capital. No gain or loss, whatever the share price.
If Bluestem offers holders extra cash or shares to convert early, that sweetener is an expense, measured at the fair value of the extra consideration.

scenes.q: Convertible bonds with carrying amount $500,000 convert into 20,000 shares of $1 par stock worth $30. Gain or loss?
scenes.say: Quick check. Convertible bonds carried at five hundred thousand convert into twenty thousand one-dollar par shares worth thirty dollars. Gain or loss? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B, none. The book value method records no gain or loss.

videos.title: Convertible preferred and stock warrants
videos.take: Warrants issued with bonds are allocated by relative fair value; the warrant portion is equity

scenes.say: Two more ways to attract investors: convertible preferred stock, and warrants.

sub: to common: no gain or loss
scenes.say: Convertible preferred stock is equity. On conversion, the preferred stock and its paid-in capital are moved to common stock and paid-in capital. Any excess of par issued over the preferred balance reduces retained earnings.

sub: The right to buy shares at a set
price for a period of time
scenes.say: A warrant gives the holder the right to buy shares at a set price for a period of time. Bluestem attaches detachable warrants to a bond issue as a sweetener.

scenes.heading: $500,000 bonds with detachable warrants, issued at par
rows: Fair value of bonds without warrants
scenes.say: Bluestem receives $500,000. Without warrants, the bonds would be worth $480,000; the warrants trade for $20,000. The proceeds are allocated by relative fair value: $480,000 to the bonds, $20,000 to paid-in capital, stock warrants.

scenes.heading: The entry
scenes.say: The bonds start at $480,000, a $20,000 discount amortized as interest. If the warrants are exercised, their $20,000 joins the cash paid as paid-in capital. Nondetachable warrants aren't separated.

scenes.q: Bonds with detachable warrants sell for $1,020,000. FV of bonds alone $900,000; FV of warrants $120,000. Amount to warrants?
scenes.say: Quick check. Bonds with detachable warrants sell for one million twenty thousand. Fair value of the bonds alone nine hundred thousand; warrants one twenty thousand. Amount allocated to warrants? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A, $120,000: total fair value equals the price here.

videos.title: Stock options: measurement
videos.take: Measure options at grant-date fair value and expense it over the service period

scenes.say: To keep its designers after the IPO, Bluestem grants them stock options.

sub: The right to buy shares at a fixed
scenes.say: An employee stock option gives the right to buy shares at a fixed exercise price, usually after a vesting period of continued service.

scenes.heading: The grant, January 1, 2029
scenes.say: On January 1, 2029, Bluestem grants 20,000 options at an exercise price of $16, equal to the market price. An option-pricing model values each option at $5. Total compensation cost is $100,000, recognized over the two-year service period.

sub: Even if the options are 'at the money',
scenes.say: Even with no intrinsic value at grant, an option is worth something: the chance the price rises. GAAP requires measuring that fair value at the grant date. It isn't remeasured later.

sub: Estimate them, or account for them
as they occur: a policy choice
scenes.say: Companies either estimate expected forfeitures from employees who'll leave before vesting, or account for forfeitures as they occur. It's an accounting policy choice.

scenes.q: 30,000 options, fair value $4 each, 3-year service period. Annual compensation expense?
scenes.say: Quick check. Thirty thousand options, fair value four dollars each, three-year service period. Annual compensation expense? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Stock options: recording
videos.take: Expense builds paid-in capital, stock options; at exercise it moves to common stock with the cash

scenes.say: Here's how the designers' options move through the books.

scenes.heading: December 31, 2029 and 2030
scenes.say: Each year of the service period, Bluestem records $50,000 of compensation expense and credits Paid-in Capital, Stock Options. No cash changes hands: employees are paid in equity.

scenes.heading: Exercise of all 20,000 options
rows: Paid-in capital in excess of par
scenes.say: When the designers exercise, they pay $16 a share, $320,000. That cash, plus the $100,000 already in Paid-in Capital, Stock Options, is credited to common stock at par and paid-in capital: $420,000 in total.

sub: Move the balance to paid-in capital
scenes.say: If the share price stays below $16 and the vested options expire, the expense isn't reversed. The balance moves to Paid-in Capital from Expired Stock Options.
Companies long fought expensing options. But options are pay, and leaving them out made profits look higher. Expensing them gives a faithful representation of the cost of employees.

scenes.q: Options with $60,000 in paid-in capital, stock options, are exercised for $240,000 cash. Total credited to common stock and paid-in capital?
scenes.say: Quick check. Options with sixty thousand in paid-in capital, stock options, are exercised for two forty thousand cash. Total credited to common stock and paid-in capital? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Restricted stock and purchase plans
videos.take: Restricted stock is expensed at grant-date fair value over vesting; discounted employee purchase plans may be compensatory

scenes.say: Bluestem's new CFO, Maria Okafor, prefers restricted stock to options.

sub: forfeited if they leave before vesting
scenes.say: Restricted stock, or restricted stock units, transfer shares to employees that vest over time and are forfeited if the employee leaves early. Unlike options, they keep value even if the price falls.

scenes.heading: Maria's grant
rows: Fair value per share at grant
scenes.say: Maria receives 4,000 restricted stock units when the share price is $15: $60,000 of compensation, recognized over four years of vesting, $15,000 a year.

Employee stock purchase plans let all employees buy shares, often at a discount. If the discount is small, around five percent or less, and the plan is broad-based, it's not compensatory. Bigger discounts are compensation expense.
Stock appreciation rights pay the increase in share price. If they're settled in cash, they're a liability remeasured to fair value every period, so expense moves with the share price.

scenes.q: 6,000 restricted shares, fair value $20 at grant, vesting over 3 years. Annual expense?
scenes.say: Quick check. Six thousand restricted shares, fair value twenty dollars at grant, vesting over three years. Annual expense? Pause and pick.

videos.title: Midterm review: Lectures 1 to 7
videos.take: Intangibles, liabilities and equity: what Bluestem owns, owes, and owes its owners

scenes.say: The midterm is next week. Here's the first half of Intermediate Accounting Two in two minutes.

scenes.heading: Intangibles and liabilities
scenes.say: We covered intangibles, R&D and goodwill impairment; current liabilities, contingencies, warranties and asset retirement obligations; bond pricing and the effective-interest method; and notes, early extinguishment and the fair value option.

scenes.heading: Equity
scenes.say: Then equity: issuing shares and treasury stock; preferred stock and dividend preferences; stock dividends and splits; and dilutive securities and stock-based pay.

One principle ties the equity lectures together: transactions with owners, like buying back shares or converting bonds, never create gains or losses. Paying employees in shares does create an expense.
For the exam, practice bond amortization tables and treasury stock entries. They're perennial favorites.
Last quick check. Which of these creates an expense? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C, employee stock options. Good luck on the midterm.

case: Bluestem must choose how to reward six key designers: (A) 30,000 stock options, exercise price $16, fair value $5 each, 3-year vesting; (B) 10,000 restricted stock units at $15, 3-year vesting; (C) a cash bonus of $50,000 a year. The founder prefers options because 'they don't cost anything unless the stock rises'.
Compute annual expense under each option.
Which plan keeps value for designers if the share price falls?
Effect of each on dilution and cash.

A: 150,000 ÷ 3 = 50,000; B: 150,000 ÷ 3 = 50,000; C: 50,000. Options are expensed at grant-date fair value regardless; the claim is wrong for accounting and for shareholders (dilution). RSUs keep value if price falls. A and B dilute and use no cash (A brings in cash at exercise); C uses cash and doesn't dilute.
exam: Explain the accounting for employee stock options from grant to exercise or expiration.
Grant-date fair value; expense over service period with credit to PIC-SO; forfeitures policy; exercise: cash + PIC-SO to CS and APIC; expiration: PIC-expired; no remeasurement.
Record the issuance at par of $500,000 of bonds with detachable warrants (bond FV $480,000, warrant FV $20,000) and later exercise of all warrants for 10,000 shares at $20 ($1 par).
